title: Howard McGhee's Finale Club band
summary: McGhee's house where the Treniers lived, and the Finale Club band with Parker, Criss, Montgomery and Edwards during the recording ban.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Later on, Howard McGhee formed a band to go into a club on First Street called the Finale Club. It was an after-hour club...

But anyway, before that... Howard had lots of records, Classical records or Jazz records, all the latest things, you know. So a lot of people used to hang there and listen to the sides all the time. It was like a music house. The Treniers were living right across the walkway in their place, the Trenier Twins and all their gang. Moses Brown became one of my real great friends later on in life, and Gene Gilbo(?), the piano player and orchestrator who was with them.

But anyway, we all used to hang around through there. And so, Howard formed this band to go into the Finale Club on First and San Pedro. The personnel was Earl (?) on piano, Bob Kesterson, bass, and Roy Porter, drums. And we had Gene Montgomery on tenor, Sonny Criss on alto, Charlie Parker on the other alto, and I'm on the tenor. That was the saxophone section. It was too bad this band wasn't recorded. It was during the recording ban. Do you remember the recording ban, when they struck, the American Federation of Musicians wouldn't let the musicians record -- they were dealing with the record companies and what have you.
We had a vocalist named Bill Jones. Now, do you remember Bill Jones?
Right, the one you know. Right, right, he's been on the scene. He was a fine singer during those days, you know.
Yeah, he was very good. In fact, he stayed with the band for a good while.
